chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, who said:
I heard Aba Ja'far عليه السلام saying:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not perform any salat during the day until the sun declined. When the day had declined by about half a finger’s measure, he performed eight rak'ahs. When the shadow reached one cubit, he performed the Zuhr salat. Then after Zuhr he performed two rak'ahs, and before the time of 'Asr he would perform two rak'ahs. When the shadow reached two cubits, he performed the 'Asr salat. He performed the Maghrib salat when the sun set. When the twilight disappeared, the time of 'Isha' began, and the end of the time of Maghrib was the return of the twilight. When the twilight returned, the time of 'Isha' began, and the end of the time of 'Isha' was one-third of the night. He would not perform salat after 'Isha' until the middle of the night; then he would perform thirteen rak'ahs, including al-Watr, and including the two rak'ahs of Fajr before al-Ghadah. When dawn rose and brightened, he performed al-Ghadah.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow connected to the timing of Maghrib and 'Isha'
key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ: the night salat performed after the disappearance of twilight
key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: the morning salat, meaning Salat al-Fajr
key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: the returning shadow used as a measure for prayer times
key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: the Watr prayer included within the night prayers
key_terms.تَزُولَ: to decline from the zenith, referring to the sun passing midday
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: one cubit, a length used here to mark the time of Zuhr
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْنِ: two cubits, a length used here to mark the time of 'Asr

ai.seo_question: What were the prayer times and daily salat routine of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله regarding the times of the daily salat and the recommended nawafil prayers surrounding them. It is significant in showing the prophetic sunnah for Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib, 'Isha', and the night prayer, and in outlining the temporal markers used for these acts of worship.
